summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 15.1% to INR387.8 crores and FY26 total income reached INR1,499.8 crores, with Dombivli opened ahead of schedule.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR387.8 crores (up 15.1%), EBITDA of INR89.2 crores (23% margin) and PAT of INR50.2 crores (up 11.5%). For FY26, total income was INR1,499.8 crores (up 15.2%), EBITDA INR343.3 crores (up 14.4%, 22.9% margin) and PAT INR194.2 crores. Dombivli, the first greenfield hospital since listing, was inaugurated in February 2026, about two months before the call. Management outlined a pipeline taking capacity from about 1,200 to nearly 3,000 beds, including a 400-bed BKC hospital, with funding planned from internal accruals and debt capped at 3x EBITDA.

segments.name: Thane
segments.commentary: Occupancy about 75%; growth expected to be inflation-linked at current capacity, with an expansion awaiting final approvals.

segments.name: Pune
segments.commentary: Occupancy close to 65% with headroom to grow; Pune South is on track to open in calendar 2028.

segments.name: Indore
segments.commentary: Occupancy 45-50% after last year's added capacity; ramp-up driven by occupancy and case mix; second phase of 111 beds to be triggered when occupancy nears 60%.

segments.name: Dombivli (new, greenfield)
segments.commentary: Opened February 2026 with 750,000 sq ft built, 500-bed superstructure and about 300 beds fitted out; expected EBITDA burn INR2-3 crores per month on average in FY27, with breakeven targeted by end of calendar 2027/2028; INR9.4 crores Dombivli contribution is included in Q4 results.

guidance_outlook: Dombivli: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month on average for the full year; EBITDA breakeven expected at end of two years of operation (calendar 2027-28).
Dombivli insurance tie-ups expected in 6-12 months, linked to NABH accreditation that needs about six months of operating data.
Pune South to open in calendar 2028; Mira Road expected to start excavation by end of calendar 2026.
Thane expansion approvals expected in FY27; scope and scale to be disclosed once final approvals are received.
Land payment for BKC: 25% of land cost paid; management said the remainder would be paid within this financial year.
Capacity target of about 1,700 new beds in this cycle, taking long-term capacity to nearly 3,000 beds at an average capex of about INR1.5 crores per bed.
Funding: internal accruals over next 4-5 years plus debt capped at 3x EBITDA considered sufficient; detailed calculations to follow.
Base business growth: Thane inflation-linked; Pune inflation plus occupancy; Indore occupancy, inflation and case mix. Management declined to quantify growth given inflation uncertainty.
capex_capacity: Dombivli opened February 2026, ahead of the Q1 FY27 target, on time and on budget with no cost escalation.
BKC: 400-bed quaternary care hospital on over 1 lakh sq ft in BKC; land allotted by MMRDA, with regulatory clearance and possession formalities underway.
Mira Road: architectural drawings complete, regulatory clearances in progress, excavation expected by end of calendar 2026.
Pune South on track for calendar 2028 opening; all projects are greenfield, full-scale hubs in Mumbai and Pune on owned real estate.
Indore phase two (111 beds) on hold until occupancy reaches around 60%.
demand_pricing: ARPOB rose 11.7% YoY to INR67,700 in Q4; drivers cited were Indore case-mix maturity and insurance renewals (roughly every two years) giving price increases plus inflation.
Insurance is 55.4% of revenue; government 1%. Insurance renewals are rolling with no single season.
International medical tourism is very small; management said it is not a focus and is not margin accretive, preferring domestic and local demand within a 45-minute drive radius.
Cost watch items: depreciating rupee and capex cost inflation; doctor costs and consumables not yet materially impacted by global supply chain disruption.
Management referred to a current war situation as a factor limiting inflation visibility.

qa_highlights.question: How is Dombivli ramping in occupancy and revenue, and when will the major insurance tie-up happen?
qa_highlights.answer: Only about two months of operations, so occupancy is too early to quantify; insurance tie-ups are linked to NABH accreditation and are likely in 6-12 months.

qa_highlights.question: How will capex and funding for the expansion to about 2,900 beds be managed over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal accruals over the next 5 years plus some debt, with a self-imposed ceiling of 3x EBITDA, should cover it.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy and ARPOB by unit, and can the base business grow more than 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Thane about 75% occupancy, Pune close to 65%, Indore 45-50%. Growth is inflation-linked plus occupancy and case mix; no numeric guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the ARPOB increase during the year?
qa_highlights.answer: A combination of Indore maturing with better case mix, and insurance renewals after a two-year cycle giving price increases plus inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Will Dombivli add fixed costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, more fixed costs are expected as doctor hiring continues over the next couple of years for a large facility.

qa_highlights.question: Share of revenue from foreign patients and the government's medical tourism push?
qa_highlights.answer: Very little foreign revenue; management is not focused on international medical tourism and does not see it as margin accretive.

risks_watch: Dombivli ramp-up: EBITDA burn of INR2-3 crores per month and rising fixed costs until breakeven; insurance empanelment and NABH accreditation timing.
Funding load from BKC and the wider pipeline (about 1,700 beds, average INR1.5 crores per bed); rupee depreciation and capex cost inflation.
Indore: occupancy still 45-50%, and the second phase depends on occupancy reaching about 60%.
Regulatory approvals for Thane expansion and BKC/Mira Road site clearances (MMRDA possession formalities) remain pending, with no firm dates.
Insurance renewals rolling through the year, with the 55.4% insurance mix exposing the business to tariff negotiations.
Management declined to guide base business growth beyond inflation-linked, citing war-related inflation uncertainty.
summary.management_tone: Confident on delivery, citing Dombivli opening early and on budget, but cautious on macro, declining to quantify inflation or base-business growth and deferring capex and occupancy numbers until more data is available.
key_quotes: We set ourselves a target of commissioning it by Q1 FY27, and I'm very pleased that we beat that and opened ahead of schedule.
We are not trying to just grow fast. We are trying to grow right.
This is an asset-heavy model by deliberate choice.
I don't want to take a guess of how inflation will play out.
